newsitem.title: USA: Hefty Clinton budget at the printers.
newsitem.headline: Hefty Clinton budget at the printers.

text.p: At the Government Printing Office Monday, President Clinton's new budget was no light matter.
One set of budget books, with marbled dark green covers, weighed in at about 10 pounds. It will be publicly unveiled Thursday.

White House Budget Director Franklin Raines stopped in at the printing site and joked that the colour of the budget books was the biggest decision the director of the Office of Management and Budget gets to make. "It looks great," he said, leafing through a volume of the "Analytical Perspectives."
The fiscal year 1998 budget will be available to the public at noon EST Thursday at the Government Printing Office and at 10 a.m. online at the www.access.gpo.gov address, a spokeswoman said.
About 110,000 soft-cover budget books will be printed. A full set of the six books to be released Thursday contained 2,484 pages and can be purchased for $151.25, while the CD-ROM version was $16.
A seventh book, the economic report of the president, will be available next week.

Security will be tight at the printing office until the budget is publicly released, spokeswoman Barbara Shaw said. "It's embargoed. They'll have people watching it day and night until Thursday," she said.
The president's budget is the largest one-time job that the printing office does each year, she added.
Copies of the "Analytical Perspectives" book rolled through binding equipment before being boxed and carried off in piles by forklifts.
"It's a good budget. It meets the president's stated goal of balancing by 2002," Raines said. "I think it will be a budget that will be well received."
The budget director joked with some of the staff working on the equipment that he would have to memorise all the pages because he had to testify before Congress on the budget Friday.
